title: Stage 7 — Final Production Readiness + Release Candidate Audit
head: d38b3ea
summary: Independent release-candidate audit. All Stage 6 fixes (BUG-1..5) independently re-verified. Found and fixed one new real defect (SSE real-time messaging authentication was unreachable — every EventSource connection returned 401) plus one minor correctness fix (malformed JSON now returns 400). Remaining items are environmental (AI with a real key, object storage against a live sidecar, live production DB — all CONFIGURATION BLOCKED), browser E2E (UNVERIFIED), and a few LOW/informational non-blocking findings.

new_defects_found_and_fixed.description: router.use(requireAuth) returned 401 before the ?token= fallback ran, and the handler used CommonJS require('../lib/auth') in an ESM module. The frontend connects via EventSource with ?token= (EventSource cannot set the Authorization header), so real-time messaging always returned 401 and never worked.
new_defects_found_and_fixed.proof: After fix: member ?token= -> 200 text/event-stream, non-member -> 403, no token -> 401, invalid token -> 401. Regression test sse-auth.test.ts (4 tests).

new_defects_found_and_fixed.description: Global error handler always returned 500, even for client errors (malformed JSON body has err.status=400). Now respects 4xx status codes.
new_defects_found_and_fixed.proof: Malformed JSON -> 400 'Invalid request' with no internals leaked. Regression test added.

remaining_findings.description: GET /api/social/posts/personalized ignores the `type` query param; the frontend requests ?type=post but clips can appear in the posts tab. Cosmetic filtering inconsistency.
cookie-parser is declared but unused; google-auth-library is a direct dep that is only used transitively by @google-cloud/storage. Harmless; left as-is per smallest-change policy.
express-rate-limit uses the in-memory store (per-process). Acceptable for single-instance Replit; needs a distributed store (e.g. Redis) for multi-instance deployments.

Disallowed cross-origin requests surface as 500 'Internal server error' via the generic handler rather than a clean 403. No Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is emitted, so browsers still block the response. Cosmetic, not a security bypass.

ai_failure_modes.invalid_key: VERIFIED (server boots, no key leak in errors, controlled failures, non-AI works, lazy init preserved)
